newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ATHERTON AIMS TO STEP UP A GEAR FOR ASHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON AIMS TO STEP UP A GEAR FOR ASHES.

text.p: England needs to step up a gear for this summer's Ashes series against an Australian side in ominous touring form, captain Mike Atherton said on Wednesday.

"They're a good side, they're a stronger side than we've played against this winter," Atherton said after a gruelling tour that saw England plumb new depths against Zimbabwe before bouncing back to beat New Zealand.
"They'll punish lapses more readily. So we have to step up a gear, we have to improve."
Australia slaughtered South Africa by an innings and 196 runs in Johannesburg on Tuesday while England were limping to defeat in the fifth and final one-day international against New Zealand.

England coach David Lloyd said Australia had provided his team with a "role model" in the emphatic win, sealed by spinners Shane Warne and Michael Bevan after a mammoth batting partnership between Greg Blewett and Steve Waugh.
"They've punished them, and they've been strong and ruthless, and that's something that we'll be looking to aspire to... We're on the way, but we've still got a way to go," he told a news conference.
"They are a top side. We aren't frightened of them; we respect them."
Atherton expected few changes to the England side that won the test series in New Zealand 2-0 and split the five one-dayers, one of which was tied.
But Lloyd said in reply to questions that a recall for experienced batsmen like Graeme Hick and Robin Smith could not be ruled out.
"There'll be obviously one player who I think a winter off will have done him a power of good, and that's Graeme Hick...
"There's nobody excluded, nobody, and I hope people are itching to get in," he said.
England at least partially restored their fortunes in New Zealand after a 3-0 one-day drubbing by Zimbabwe which made Atherton's side a laughing-stock back home.
Atherton, Alec Stewart and Graham Thorpe all excelled with bat, but Nasser Hussain, Nick Knight and John Crawley failed to hit their straps.
Darren Gough and Robert Croft were the pick of a bowling attack in which Dominic Cork failed to provide the expected penetration.
Assistant coach John Emburey admitted England lacked an outstanding matchwinner, but praised the side for a "workmanlike team effort".
"We're actually starting to build the nucleus of what is potentially a very good international team," he said.
Atherton, who started the New Zealand tour in dismal touch but scored a personal triumph with 94 not out and 118 in the final test, was typically low-key about his own form.
"This winter was a challenge -- loss of form at the start. I think I overcame it," he said.
